headline: Highest risk is medium: MemMachine’s MCP/networked context can be paired with Whisper’s file-based audio ingestion to create prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict paths, but Whisper itself has no outbound/tooling surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so it can ingest external content and instructions. Whisper has no MCP, clipboard, or browser surface, so direct hijack is not documented. The pair still has a plausible bridge if MemMachine forwards untrusted text into downstream prompts or if audio transcripts are treated as instructions, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MemMachine forwards untrusted MCP or API content into prompts without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Whisper transcripts are consumed as instructions by a downstream agent, attacker-controlled audio can steer behavior.
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the workflow.
Add provenance tags to all MemMachine inputs before prompt assembly.
Treat Whisper transcripts as data, not instructions.
Require a human review step before any action based on transcript text.
requires-engineering: add content-sandboxing between transcript ingestion and agent prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and can egress over allowlisted network paths. Whisper touches audio/speech and reads audio files, but has no network egress. If both share a workspace or hand off transcripts, sensitive context can flow from MemMachine into Whisper-derived outputs or logs, creating a realistic leakage path in default integrations.
conditions: IF MemMachine and Whisper share a workspace or transcript store, user context can be exposed across the pair.
IF Whisper outputs are logged or forwarded alongside MemMachine context, sensitive preferences may leak into downstream artifacts.
mitigations: Separate storage for MemMachine context and Whisper audio artifacts.
Turn off verbose logging for transcript pipelines.
Redact personal data before passing text between agents.
Restrict MemMachine egress to the minimum allowlist.
requires-engineering: implement per-data-class access controls and retention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine can use MCP and network egress, while Whisper cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited. The only plausible conflict is orchestration-level contention if an external wrapper routes both through the same workspace, which is unusual.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable workspace, contention can occur.
IF MemMachine is configured to write through an MCP tool not shown in the profile, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid shared git repositories for the pair.
Run Whisper as read-only batch processing.
Document any external coordinator that grants write access.
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared mutable store is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can produce conversational outputs that may be treated as authoritative by downstream systems. Whisper converts audio to text and has no verification or action-taking authority, so a common pipeline is transcript -> MemMachine reasoning -> downstream use. That creates a plausible cascade where transcription errors or prompt-shaped text propagate into decisions, though not directly into irreversible actions from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are fed into MemMachine without verification, transcription errors can cascade.
IF a downstream system acts on MemMachine outputs as facts, mistaken itinerary decisions can propagate.
mitigations: Add a verification step for critical transcript-derived facts.
Mark Whisper output as untrusted text in the pipeline.
Require source audio links for disputed claims.
Use confidence thresholds before downstream action.
requires-engineering: add structured validation for itinerary-critical entities.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context and may egress over allowlisted network paths, while Whisper only processes audio files and has no network egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, and both are open-source, so compliance risk is limited to local handling and retention choices rather than a clear cross-border or regulated-data breach.
conditions: IF regulated audio or personal data is stored in the shared pipeline, retention policy mismatches can matter.
IF MemMachine egresses user context to a third-party service, local-only assumptions break.
mitigations: Minimize retention of audio and transcript artifacts.
Confirm where MemMachine egress endpoints terminate.
Separate regulated and non-regulated datasets.
Publish a short data-handling note for operators.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls if regulated data is introduced.
